Package hadur2.core.move

Class SurfMover

java.lang.Object
hadur2.core.move.SurfMover
public class SurfMover extends Object
The duel's wave surfing: each tick, decides where to drive so that the enemy's next bullets are least likely to hit us, and writes the body's turn, distance and speed into the orders.

Where it sits in the tick. HadurCore calls move(hadur2.core.model.BotOrders.Builder, hadur2.core.model.RobotState, hadur2.core.move.MoveController, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, int, boolean) once a duel tick, after MoveController has broken passed waves and updated the bullet shadows, or ram(hadur2.core.model.BotOrders.Builder, hadur2.core.model.RobotState, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double) instead while the enemy is disabled (END-2). The distance policy sets setDesiredDistance(double) every tick (DIST-1, END-1) and the movement flavour sets setMode(hadur2.core.move.SurfMover.Mode) (MOVE-2). With no firing wave in the air it orbits the enemy.

How a wave is surfed. For the first surfable wave, each option (orbit counter-clockwise, stop, orbit clockwise, or in go-to mode a spread of stop points) is simulated tick by tick with the engine's own movement rules (MovementPredictor) until the wave passes our centre. The states in which the wave is crossing us give the precise intersection: the firing angles that would hit us. Its danger is the views' score there (MoveController.getDangerScore(hadur2.core.model.Wave, hadur2.core.model.Wave.Intersection, int), which counts only the part our bullets do not shadow, MOVE-1 and MOVE-3), times the bullet's damage, over the ticks until impact, and scaled by whether the move takes us closer to the enemy. With two waves to surf, the second wave's best option from where the first leaves us is added, so the choice for the first wave does not corner us for the next. The cheapest option wins.

Orbit and distance. Each orbit heads perpendicular to the line from the enemy, bent by an attack angle toward the enemy when we are further than the desired distance and away when nearer, capped at 0.45 pi. Near a wall the heading is wall-smoothed: turned along the wall, keeping the orbit's direction, so neither the prediction nor the drive heads into it.

Angles are radians on Robocode's compass (0 north, clockwise); distances in px; times in ticks. SurfMover.SurfOption.direction is +1 for clockwise, -1 for counter-clockwise, as seen from above with y up. State kept between ticks is the option and destination chosen for the wave being surfed, so the choice does not flicker; it resets when a new wave is surfed and at each round.

    • checkDanger

      double checkDanger(RobotState myState, MoveController moveCtrl, RobotState startState, SurfMover.SurfOption option, boolean prevClockwise, int surfWaveIndex, int numWaves, double cutoff, RobotStateLog predictedLog)
      The danger of taking option against the surfWaveIndex-th surfable wave from startState, plus (while surfWaveIndex + 1 < numWaves and this wave's danger is under cutoff) the least danger of the three options against the next wave from where this one leaves us.

      The drive is simulated tick by tick toward the option's destination, at full speed (or 0 for a stop), until the wave reaches our centre. From the first tick the wave's front touches our hit box, the states are also played forward as if we braked there, until the wave has wholly passed: those are the states the wave can hit, and their precise intersection is what waveDanger(hadur2.core.model.RobotState, hadur2.core.move.MoveController, hadur2.core.model.Wave, int, java.util.List<hadur2.core.model.RobotState>, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double, java.awt.geom.Point2D.Double) scores.

      Parameters:
      myState - our real state now, which fixes which waves are surfable and their time to impact
      moveCtrl - the waves and danger views
      startState - where this leg of the prediction starts
      option - the option to simulate
      prevClockwise - the orbit side a stop is smoothed along
      surfWaveIndex - which surfable wave, 0 the first
      numWaves - how many waves to look ahead in all
      cutoff - the best total so far; the next wave is skipped when this one alone is not below it
      predictedLog - the states predicted on earlier legs, to replay against a later wave that was already crossing us during them; this leg's states are added to it
      Returns:
      the danger, 0 when there is no such wave or it has already passed

    • goToCandidates

      List<Point2D.Double> goToCandidates(RobotState myState, Wave surfWave)
      The stop points: where we stand, and every few ticks along both orbits until the wave passes.

      Each orbit is predicted at full speed toward that side's precise escape point (the furthest round the source we could get before the wave arrives, with the attack angle toward the desired distance), wall-smoothed; a point is taken every GO_TO_SPACING ticks and at the tick the wave reaches our centre, which is where the orbit ends. So the candidates span everything from standing still to going all out either way.

      Parameters:
      myState - our state now
      surfWave - the wave being surfed
      Returns:
      the candidates, our own position first

    • distancingDanger

      double distancingDanger(Point2D.Double start, Point2D.Double predicted, Point2D.Double enemy)
      How much a move from start to predicted scales a wave's danger for its change in distance to enemy: 2.5^(d0 / d1) / 2.5, where d0 is the distance before and d1 after. Holding the distance gives 1; halving it gives 2.5; doubling it about 0.63. So among equally safe moves the surf prefers the ones that do not close in.
      Parameters:
      start - where the move starts, in px
      predicted - where it ends, in px
      enemy - the wave's source, in px
      Returns:
      the factor, above 0
